question: Maximum how many overs can a bowler bowl in ODI cricket matches?
solution:
The correct answer is __**10.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

 
• 
 
**ODI:-**

 
 
• 
 
It stands for "One Day International," which is a format of limited-overs cricket.

 
 
• 
 
In ODI cricket, each team faces a set number of overs, typically 50 overs per side, to bat and bowl. ODI matches are played over a single day, as opposed to Test matches, which can last up to five days. 

 
 
• 
 
**In One Day International (ODI) cricket matches, a bowler can bowl a maximum of 10 overs in a single innings.**

 
 
• 
 
This rule is designed to ensure fairness and to prevent any single bowler from dominating the match by consistently bowling long spells.
